segments.title: Pandemic governance — emergency as operating system
segments.narration: Public health orders, economic transfers, and procurement under emergency conditions redefine the citizen-state interface. ArriveCAN becomes the emblematic digital failure. The film holds AG findings and parliamentary scrutiny as the spine — not social media rumor.

segments.title: ArriveCAN — cost overrun as case study
segments.narration: A border app balloons far beyond initial estimates. GC Strategies and related contracting enter the public scandal lexicon. Auditor General work and committee testimony freeze the numbers. This is the digital-state failure lineage after Phoenix.

segments.title: Freedom Convoy and the Emergencies Act
segments.narration: Protest, occupation, and the first use of the Emergencies Act in its modern form produce a commission record and lasting polarization. Banking freezes and police powers become permanent political memory. Primary documents: proclamation, commission evidence, court challenges.

segments.title: Bill C-7 — MAID expansion under pandemic parliament
segments.narration: Eligibility expands beyond reasonably foreseeable death. Track two begins. Health Canada reports document rising counts. Disability advocates warn of structural coercion via poverty and care gaps — warnings the film preserves as contemporaneous dissent on the record.

segments.title: Housing shock — rates, supply, and financialization
segments.narration: Pandemic migration, low rates then hikes, investor demand, and chronic undersupply produce a generational affordability break. CMHC and Statistics Canada series are the primary instruments. Announced billions versus delivered units become a permanent gap chart on this site.

segments.title: Pandemic powers and ArriveCAN
segments.narration: Emergency orders, border apps, and procurement explode. ArriveCAN becomes the Auditor General's emblem of cost overrun. Phoenix pay already proved payroll failure; ArriveCAN proves app failure. Same pattern, different decade.

segments.title: Bill C-7 — MAID expansion
segments.narration: Bill C-7 expands MAID beyond reasonably foreseeable natural death and sets the track for mental illness alone. Disability advocates warn. Hansard and committee evidence preserve the warnings. The death counts that follow are Health Canada's numbers.

segments.title: Emergencies Act — convoy and inquiry
segments.narration: The federal Emergencies Act is invoked for the first time. Banks freeze. The Rouleau commission later rules the threshold met — a finding critics dispute. Primary order-in-council text, commission transcripts, and court challenges are the record. Social media of officials and organizers is public secondary evidence.
